Describe which columns vary within a unit

Source: R/describe_varying.R
describe_varying.Rd

Some columns should be constant within a unit: sex and birth date per person, the start year of a company. Others are expected to vary: income, address. describe_varying() shows, for each column, how many units have more than one value, so the constant columns, the varying ones and the nearly constant ones stand apart. A column that varies for a handful of units out of millions is rarely meant to vary: those units are usually errors, and ensure_constant() lists them.

Usage

describe_varying(data, id, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database tables in checkpoints.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select), e.g. cpr.

...

Columns to describe (tidy-select). Defaults to all other columns.

Value

An object of class inshape_varying, printed as a summary. It is a list with ids, n_units and columns, a tibble with one row per column: column, varying (units with more than one non-missing value), share (of the units with a value), partly_missing (units with both missing and non-missing values) and all_missing, sorted from the most constant to the most varying.

Details

A missing value is not counted as a value of its own: a person whose sex is missing in one year and known in another has not changed sex, but is partly missing, which is counted separately.

It is the within-unit view of Stata's xtsum, for categories as well as numbers.

Why it is fast

Units are grouped once by the compiled engine (see checkpoints). For each column, one compiled pass compares every row with the first non-missing value of its unit, with no hashing or sorting of the column and one memory word of state per unit.

See also

ensure_constant() to require a column to be constant within units and list the units that break it.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c"),
  year   = c(2020, 2021, 2020, 2021, 2020, 2021),
  sex    = c("F", "F", "M", "F", "M", NA),
  income = c(100, 120, 90, 95, 80, 85)
)
describe_varying(persons, cpr)
#> ── Within cpr ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 3 units, 3 columns
#> 
#> ✔ No column is nearly constant
#> • Constant: 0 columns
#> 
#> Per column:
#>     column varying share   partly_missing all_missing
#>   1 sex          1 33.33%               1           0
#>   2 income       3 100.00%              0           0
#>   3 year         3 100.00%              0           0
